words.etymology:
From Proto-Albanian *mal̄, from Pre-Proto-Albanian *malnə, from Proto-Indo-European *mĺ̥h₃nu- (“mountain”), from older *mólh₃nu- (“the emerging one”), from the root *melh₃-.
Orel's reconstruction of Proto-Albanian *mala- cannot be accepted as it would have led to Albanian *mall. For the same reason, Demiraj's reconstruction of *m(o)lH-i- cannot be accepted either.
Although the thematic precursor *mólh₃nos has found widespread acceptance, it is most likely that mal follows a u-stem precursor, *mólh₃nus, as an *-os ending should lead to an -ë ending. This also supports the plural form male, which is feminine, unlike the masculine singular.
Preserved in patronyms, ethnonym malësor (“highlander, mountaineer”), in toponym (historical and ethnographic region) Malësia (north Albania and Montenegro). In Kosovo (Malishevë, Gjilan, Mališevo, Prizren), in Serbia (Maleševo (Golubac), Maleševo (Rekovac)) and the name of Maleshevo Mountain (North Macedonia and Bulgaria).

words.etymology:
Unclear. From Old Albanian gluhë, most likely from earlier *glu.a, with sporadic loss of intervocalic b (see pi, det, and dra) and insertion of a hiatus-filling h (see bahe, kohë, and pah), from Proto-Albanian *glubā (“tip”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵlubʰeh₂- (“point”), albeit with no adduced cognates. Alternatively, from a Proto-Albanian *glusā, from Proto-Indo-European *gl̥H-so-s, a zero-grade variant of *golH-so-s, from *gelH- (“to call”); compare Proto-Balto-Slavic *galsás (“voice”).
A loan from Ancient Greek γλῶσσα (glôssa) is improbable from a semantic and phonetic standpoint, as Ancient Greek loans involved terms of trade and agriculture, not body parts, and would have given **gluśa in Proto-Albanian.
